'''Paul Reed''' (born June 14, 1999), nicknamed "'''BBall Paul'''",<ref>{{cite news|first=Justin|last=Grasso|title=Rookie Paul Reed Loves the Support From Sixers Fans|url=https://www.si.com/nba/76ers/news/rookie-paul-reed-loves-support-sixers-fans|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|access-date=April 19, 2022|date=March 20, 2021}}</ref> is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Detroit Pistons]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul Blue Demons]].

==Early life==
Reed grew up in [[Orlando, Florida]], and attended [[Wekiva High School]]. Reed grew from being 6'2" as a freshman in high school to 6'6" as a junior and was 6'8" by the start of his senior year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/os-hs-paul-reed-basketball-0730-20160729-story.html|title=Basketball report: Wekiva's Paul Reed on radar for UCF, others|first=Buddy|last=Collings|work=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|date=July 29, 2016|access-date=December 10, 2019}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 18.2 points and 11.4 rebounds and was named the [[Central Florida]] Player of the Year as he led the Mustangs to the state championship game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Article/DePaul-Officially-Inks-Paul-Reed-for-2017-74913289/|title=DePaul Officially Inks Paul Reed for 2017|website=247Sports.com|access-date=December 10, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/os-sp-hs-boys-basketball-all-area-0319-story.html|title=Paul Reed leads All-Central Florida boys basketball teams|work=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|date=March 18, 2017|access-date=December 10, 2019}}</ref> Rated a three-star recruit and the No. 235 prospect in his class, Reed committed to play college basketball at [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]] over offers from [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]], [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]], [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]] and [[Murray State Racers men's basketball|Murray State]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://thecatchandshoot.com/depaul-adds-paul-reed-to-2017-class/|title=DePaul adds 3-star Paul Reed to 2017 class|first=Jesse|last=Kramer|website=TheCatchAndShoot.com|date=December 4, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2019/12/5/20996865/depaul-basketball-ncaa-tournament-rankings-texas-tech-2020|title=DePaul basketball's dream resurgence is finally real|first=Ricky|last=O'Donnell|website=[[SB Nation]]|date=December 5, 2019|access-date=December 10, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
As a true freshman, Reed averaged 3.6 points, and 3.1 rebounds in 28 games played off the bench.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://depauliaonline.com/39318/sports/hard-work-pays-off-in-year-two-for-paul-reed/|title=Hard work pays off in year two for Paul Reed|first=Evan|last=Sully|work=The DePaulia|date=February 18, 2019|access-date=December 10, 2019}}</ref> He received more playing time towards the end of the season and averaged 5.6 points and 4.6 rebounds over the final 14 games of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://depauliaonline.com/31836/sports/unheralded-freshman-shows-late-season-promise/|title=Unheralded freshman shows late season promise|first=Paul|last=Steeno|work=The DePaulia|date=February 26, 2018|access-date=December 10, 2019}}</ref> As a sophomore, Reed - notably stimulated by the work ethic of his teammate [[Max Strus]] - <ref>{{cite web|url=https://depauliaonline.com/43838/sports/former-depaul-mens-basketball-star-lands-two-way-contract-with-bulls/|title=Former DePaul men’s basketball star lands two-way contract with Bulls|first=Shane |last=René|website=depauliaonline.com|date=October 28, 2019}} : "“(Strus) showed me what it takes,” junior forward Paul Reed said of his former teammate. “He was always in the gym before me and he was the best on our team. He showed us the way to do it.”</ref> averaged 12.3 points and a [[Big East Conference]]-leading 8.5 rebounds per game and was named the Big East Conference [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Most Improved Player|Most Improved Player]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/depaul/Article/Paul-Reed-is-Most-Improved-in-the-Big-East-129961743/|title=Paul Reed is Most Improved in the Big East|first=Steve|last=Newhouse|website=247Sports.com|date=March 11, 2019|access-date=December 10, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1439624/2019/12/06/searching-for-siakam-heres-a-big-wing-with-sleeper-potential-that-the-warriors-could-consider-in-the-2020-nba-draft/|title=Searching for Siakam: Here's a big wing with sleeper potential that the Warriors could consider in the 2020 NBA Draft|first=Ethan|last=Strauss|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=December 6, 2019|access-date=December 10, 2019}}</ref> In the [[2019 College Basketball Invitational]] Reed averaged 18.3 points, 10.3 rebounds, 2.7 blocks, and 2.2 steals as he helped lead the Blue Demons to the best-of-three final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2019/10/15/big-east-basketball-20-interesting-people-2019-20-season/3/|title=Big East Basketball: 20 most interesting people of 2019-20 season|first=Brian|last=Foley|website=BustingBrackets.com|publisher=FanSided|date=October 15, 2019|access-date=December 10, 2019}}</ref>

Reed entered his junior season as a preseason All-Big East selection.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hoopshype.com/2019/12/09/depaul-paul-reed-scouting-report-nba-draft-analysis/|title=DePaul big man Paul Reed is one of NCAA's most underrated prospects|first=Bryan|last=Kalbrosky|website=Hoops Hype|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=December 9, 2019|access-date=December 10, 2019}}</ref> Reed recorded ten double-doubles and was named to the Big East Weekly Honor Roll four times during DePaul's 13-game non-conference schedule at the start of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/depaul/Article/DePauls-Paul-Reed-Blossoming-in-Junior-Season-140241445/|title=DePaul's Paul Reed Blossoming in Junior Season|first=Scott|last=Phillips|website=247Sports.com|date=December 10, 2019|access-date=December 23, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://depaulbluedemons.com/news/2019/12/16/mens-basketball-big-east-honors-paul-reed-once-again.aspx|title=BIG EAST Honors Paul Reed Once Again|website=DePaulBlueDemons.com|date=December 16, 2019|access-date=December 23, 2019}}</ref> Reed scored 23 points on 8-of-9 shooting with nine rebounds in DePaul's 79–66 upset of No. 5 [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]] on January 18.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/2020/01/18/depaul-upsets-top-five-butler-paul-reed|title=Paul Reed's 23 Points Lead DePaul to Upset Over No. 5 Butler|website=[[Sports Illustrated|SI.com]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 18, 2020|access-date=February 3, 2020}}</ref> Reed missed several games in February and March with a hip pointer injury.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Newhouse |first1=Steve |title=Providence Routs DePaul |url=https://247sports.com/college/depaul/Article/Providence-Friars-Rout-DePaul-Blue-Demons-on-Senior-Day-144738988/ |access-date=March 8, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=March 7, 2020}}</ref> After the regular season, Reed was named Second Team All-Big East after averaging 15.1 points and finishing second in the conference in rebounds (10.7), blocks (2.6) and steals (1.9).<ref>{{cite news |last1=Baum |first1=Adam |title=Xavier basketball players honored on All-Big East Conference teams |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/2020/03/08/xavier-basketball-gets-4-players-all-conference-team/4994440002/ |access-date=March 8, 2020 |work=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]] |date=March 8, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/depaul/Article/DePauls-Paul-Reed-Named-All-Big-East-Second-Team-144779680/|title=DePaul's Paul Reed Named All-Big East Second Team|first=Steve|last=Newhouse|website=247Sports.com|date=March 8, 2020|access-date=March 16, 2020}}</ref> He had 18 [[double-double]]s for the season. After the season, Reed declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]], forgoing his final season of eligibility.<ref>{{cite news |title=DePaul junior Paul Reed declares for NBA Draft |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2020/3/28/21198392/depaul-junior-paul-reed-declares-for-nba-draft |access-date=March 29, 2020 |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |date=March 28, 2020}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Philadelphia 76ers (2020–2024)===
[[File:Paul Reed.jpg|thumb|Reed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in 2022]]
Reed was drafted in the second round with 58th overall selection in the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Team Selects Tyrese Maxey, Isaiah Joe, and Paul Reed |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/team-selects-tyrese-maxey-isaiah-joe-and-paul-reed |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 4, 2020 |date=November 18, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-nba-draft-paul-reed-depaul-20201119-ifq3wavknvb3vnn57vbfsuvjmu-story.html|title=DePaul's Paul Reed drafted by Philadelphia 76ers|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=November 19, 2020|access-date=November 19, 2020}}</ref> On December 3, he signed with the 76ers on a [[two-way contract]], meaning he would split time between the 76ers and their G League affiliate, the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Team Signs Maxey, Joe, Reed |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/team-signs-maxey-joe-reed |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 4, 2020 |date=December 3, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-paul-reed-contract-76ers-basketball-nba-20201128.html|title=Sixers signing second-round draft pick Paul Reed to two-way contract|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|first=Keith|last=Pompey|date=November 28, 2020}}</ref> Reed made his NBA debut on January 4, 2021, playing the final 90 seconds of the game and scoring two points on his sole field goal attempt in a 118–101 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202101040PHI.html|title=Charlotte Hornets at Philadelphia 76ers Box Score, January 4, 2021|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 10, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-hornets-tyrese-maxey-joel-embiid-20210104.html|title=Joel Embiid's passing, Tyrese Maxey's shooting: Two more reasons to love these Sixers|first=David|last=Murphy|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=January 4, 2021|access-date=January 10, 2021}}</ref> Paul played with the [[Delaware Blue Coats|Blue Coats]] during the [[2020–21 NBA G League season|shortened single-site G League season in 2021]], where he won the league's [[NBA G League Most Valuable Player Award|Most Valuable Player]] and [[NBA G League Rookie of the Year Award|Rookie of the Year]] awards.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/delaware-blue-coats-paul-reed-named-2020-21-nba-g-league-most-valuable-player-and-rookie-of-the-year/ |title=Delaware Blue Coats' Paul Reed Named 2020-21 NBA G League Most Valuable Player And Rookie Of The Year |website=NBA G League |date=March 22, 2021}}</ref>

On March 26, 2021, the 76ers announced that they had converted Reed to a standard NBA contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=76ers Sign Paul Reed to Standard NBA Contract, Mason Jones to Two-Way Deal|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-paul-reed-standard-nba-contract-mason-jones-two-way-deal|date=March 26, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=March 26, 2021}}</ref>

On November 27, 2022, Reed grabbed 13 rebounds and scored 12 points during a win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/sixers/2022/11/28/paul-reed-discusses-improvement-as-a-roller-for-sixers-on-offense/76159577007/|title=Paul Reed discusses improvement as a roller for Sixers on offense|first=Ky|last=Carlin|website=Sixers Wire}}</ref>

On May 2, 2023, Reed sank four clutch free throws, leading the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] to win Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Semi-finals against the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-02 |title=Paul Reed talks improvement in free throws after sealing Sixers' win |url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2023/05/02/paul-reed-talks-improvement-in-free-throws-after-sealing-sixers-win/ |access-date=2023-07-13 |website=Sixers Wire |language=en-US}}</ref>

On July 8, 2023, Reed signed the [[Utah Jazz]]’s  three-year, $23 million offer sheet.<ref>{{Cite web|title=76ers free agent Paul Reed Jr. signs Jazz offer sheet|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/37978331/76ers-free-agent-paul-reed-jr-signs-jazz-offer-sheet|date=July 8, 2023|website=ESPN.com|access-date=July 9, 2023}}</ref> The [[Philadelphia 76ers]] matched that offer sheet the next day.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sixers match Reed's offer sheet, keep him in Philadelphia|url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nba/philadelphia-76ers/sixers-match-paul-reed-offer-sheet-daryl-morey-nba/526832/?amp=1|date=July 9, 2023|website=NBCSportsPhiladelphia.com|access-date=July 9, 2023}}</ref>

On January 27, 2024, Reed posted a career-high 30 points, along with 13 rebounds in a 111–105 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jokic, Nuggets fend off gritty 76ers 111-105 as Embiid sits out for 4th consecutive time in Denver|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585272|website=ESPN.com|date=January 27, 2024|access-date=January 28, 2024}}</ref>

On July 6, 2024, Reed was waived by the 76ers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers Waive Paul Reed|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-waive-paul-reed|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 9, 2024}}</ref>

===Detroit Pistons (2024–present)===
On July 9, 2024, the [[Detroit Pistons]] claimed Reed off waivers,<ref>{{cite web|title=DETROIT PISTONS CLAIM PAUL REED OFF WAIVERS|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-claim-paul-reed-off-waivers|website=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2024|access-date=July 9, 2024}}</ref> but waived him on December 14.<ref>{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Pistons Release Paul Reed|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/12/pistons-releasing-paul-reed.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=December 14, 2024|access-date=December 14, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Sources: Pistons waive Reed to open roster spot|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/42969197/pistons-waiving-center-paul-reed-sources-say|website=ESPN.com|date=December 14, 2024|access-date=December 14, 2024}}</ref> The next day, Reed re-signed with the Pistons.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The Detroit Pistons announced today that the team has re-signed forward/center Paul Reed.|number=1868787136679625203|user=Pistons_PR|date=December 16, 2024|access-date=December 17, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=NBA News: Detroit Pistons Reunite With Paul Reed|url=https://www.si.com/nba/pistons/news/nba-news-detroit-pistons-reunite-with-paul-reed-01jf8wdksbp6|website=SI.com|date=December 16, 2024|access-date=December 17, 2024}}</ref>

On December 19, 2024, Reed started an altercation with [[Jordan Clarkson]], and was fined $15,000 on December 21.<ref>https://nba.com/jazz-pistons-penalties{{Dead link | date=August 2025 | fix-attempted=yes}}</ref>

On June 30, 2025, Reed agreed to a two-year, $11 million contract to return to the Pistons.<ref>{{cite web | last=Sankofa II | first=Omari | title=Detroit Pistons re-sign Paul Reed to two-year deal in NBA free agency | website=Detroit Free Press | date=2025-06-30 | url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2025/06/30/detroit-pistons-nba-free-agency-paul-reed-contract/84422273007/?gnt-cfr=1&gca-cat=p&gca-uir=true&gca-epti=z116437p119950c119950u115537d00----v116437&gca-ft=215&gca-ds=sophi&gnt-djm=1 | access-date=2025-12-03}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Reed's father, Paul, played college basketball at Old Dominion and UCF, then played professional basketball in Europe. He has four sisters.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Paul Reed - MEN'S BASKETBALL|url=https://depaulbluedemons.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/paul-reed/1869|access-date=2022-02-09|website=DePaul University Athletics|language=en}}</ref> His uncle, [[Mike Sims-Walker]], played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rosen |first1=Lauren |title=Quick Facts - Paul Reed |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/quick-facts-paul-reed |website=NBA |access-date=July 10, 2023 |date=November 20, 2020}}</ref>

Outside of basketball, Reed is known on [[social media]] to sell his 'Out the Mud' labelled [[Hoodie]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pompey |first=Keith |date=2023-01-06 |title=Sixers’ Paul Reed finding success off the court with his ‘Out The Mud’ hoodie sales |url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-paul-reed-out-the-mud-hoodie-20230106.html |access-date=2023-07-13 |website=www.inquirer.com |language=en}}</ref> 'Out the Mud' calls back to a tweet Paul posted when he didn't receive any playing time in a game, referencing the [[Lil Baby]] and [[Future (rapper)|Future]] [[Out the Mud|song of the same name]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=@Bball_paul: Finna have to get it out the mud again |url=https://twitter.com/Bball_paul/status/1339045219178844166?lang=en |access-date=2023-07-13 |website=Twitter |language=en}}</ref>
